estatePlan.concept: A Caribbean belvedere is composed as a deeply cut, two-storey stone-and-concrete promontory: arrival is deliberately compressed through a shaded north entry court, then released through a central dining hall to a long, sheltered south living frontage and sea terrace. The house is articulated rather than stacked: a west social-and-guest wing and east service-and-family wing brace a tall central spine, while the upper floor becomes a quieter suite level under a single low mono-pitch roof rising away from the ocean. Assumption: the site falls conceptually toward the sea to the south; all levels are nonetheless authored at a flat datum for this schematic plan.
estatePlan.character: Magazine-quality modern tropical residence: substantial pale local stone plinths, warm timber soffits and screens, board-formed architectural concrete, dark bronze detailing and carefully framed sea glazing. The architecture prioritizes deep shade, cross-ventilated perimeter rooms, protected outdoor living and a composed arrival-to-horizon sequence rather than an indiscriminate glass facade.

requirements.statement: Create an extraordinary modern tropical mansion overlooking the Caribbean Sea in Saint Lucia, with a genuinely residential and cohesive architectural composition.
The design ambition is commensurate with a $20 million luxury residence; this is a design guide and not a verified construction estimate.
Prioritize expansive ocean-facing living spaces, luxurious suites, balconies and terraces.

program.role: Primary luxury residence with social, guest, family and private suite accommodation
Sheltered entertaining terrace and infinity-edge pool composition
Formal motor arrival and pedestrian approach

architecture.intent: A central spine is recessed at arrival and projected toward the sea, giving the residence a legible hierarchy of wings, shaded recesses and a singular horizon-facing living frontage.

relationships.intent: The north gate, motor court, entry recess, foyer and central dining hall form a compressed-to-expansive arrival sequence.
The central dining hall and southern living rooms extend directly to the sea terrace and pool.
The pool is set within the broad southern terrace as the horizon amenity of the residence.

considerations.intent: Principal living rooms, family lounge and primary bedroom receive the protected southern sea frontage; service rooms occupy the more sheltered north-east edge.
Guest accommodation is buffered in the west wing and all upper bedrooms are reached from the central landing rather than through another suite.
